title: Farah Khan Says Superstar Era Is Over, Calls New Actors Insecure
excerpt: On Double Date, the filmmaker said younger actors interfere in choreography, music and casting, and named Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar as the last superstars.
body:
• Filmmaker Farah Khan said on Neha Dhupia and Angad Bedi's show Double Date that today's actors lack confidence and interfere in choreography, music and casting instead of trusting directors.
  • She named Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar as the last superstars, saying they still work as hard as when they started.
  • Farah recalled that Shah Rukh Khan never questioned her casting of Sushmita Sen in Main Hoon Na or a newcomer, Deepika Padukone, in Om Shanti Om.
  • When Angad Bedi remarked that the era of the superstar was over, Farah agreed: "Yes, we had the last of them. Enjoy them."

A director's blunt assessment

Filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan has offered a blunt assessment of how Hindi cinema works today, arguing in her view that a lack of confidence is driving younger actors to interfere in parts of filmmaking that are not their job. Speaking on Double Date, the show hosted by Neha Dhupia and Angad Bedi, Farah said actors now want a say in choreography, music and casting as well as performance.

"The problem is today's actors don't have confidence in anyone," she said, according to Indulge Express. "They don't have confidence in the director. They want to choreograph the song on their own, interfere in music and casting as well. All of this comes when you are not confident about yourself."

Bollywood Hungama reported a similar version of the same remarks. "In today's actors, nobody has confidence," Farah said. "They want to interfere everywhere. They want to do the choreography themselves, interfere in the music, direct the film themselves and interfere in casting. That comes when you are not confident about yourself. You have to trust everyone."

"Bollywood Hungama quoted her as saying: "Shah Rukh works harder, Amitabh Bachchan is working so hard on Kaun Banega Crorepati , Salman Khan works every day."

What she says an actor's job should be

Farah reserved her sharpest criticism for what she described as the basics. "That is not your job. You do your job. Learn your lines first," she said. "Your job is to know your lines when you come on set. That you are not able to do. It's irritating. I have seen it. I have done actors' first movie, and then after their fifth movie, they think they know it all. They are surrounded by people."

She also criticised what she presented as a focus on recognition before the work itself. Bollywood Hungama quoted her as saying, "Aaj kal unhein magazine ke cover pe aana hai aur award chahiye, pehle picture toh dhang se kar lo" — suggesting actors should focus on making the film properly before seeking magazine covers and awards.

"The era of superstars is over. They (Salman, SRK, Amitabh, Akshay) are the last of them; enjoy them for as long as they work."

The contrast she drew with Shah Rukh Khan

To make her point, Farah pointed to her long collaboration with Shah Rukh Khan, the star of her Hindi-language directorial debut Main Hoon Na (2004) and Om Shanti Om. She recalled that he never questioned her casting decisions, even when they were unconventional at the time.

"Shah Rukh has never interfered in casting when I said I want Sushmita Sen for Main Hoon Na even though she wasn't any big heroine," she said. "He didn't question. I said I want new girl in Om Shanti Om, he didn't question. He just saw the photo (of Deepika Padukone) and said, 'if you are fine with it, I'm fine.'"

Bollywood Hungama carried a near-identical recollection, quoting her as saying Shah Rukh told her, "If you feel so, go ahead," when shown the newcomer's picture.

Why she calls them the last superstars

Farah named four actors — Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar — as examples of a work ethic she said has endured. According to Indulge Express, she said they continue to work as hard as they did when they started out, with some putting in even more effort today. Bollywood Hungama quoted her as saying: "Shah Rukh works harder, Amitabh Bachchan is working so hard on Kaun Banega Crorepati, Salman Khan works every day. Akshay works every day and keeps everyone on their toes."

During the conversation, it was Angad Bedi who first remarked that the era of the superstar was over, according to Bollywood Hungama. Farah agreed, saying, "Yes, we had the last of them. Enjoy them."

What it means for diaspora audiences

Farah's remarks are her opinion, not an industry consensus, and no other filmmaker or actor is quoted responding to them in either report. But the debate will be familiar to diaspora audiences who grew up on the star-driven Hindi cinema of Shah Rukh, Salman, Amitabh and Akshay — and who now watch a more fragmented, streaming-led industry. Whether a new generation can command the same single-name draw is the question her comments leave open.
